answer: The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. Potter guild membership with kiln firing history is the check: firing histories filed with one guild chapter for years. The price is per head, and the shale test proves it: A farm faking 413 aliases needs 413 separate firing histories, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. The knoll trail is public, the pearl check is cheap to run, and a farm of 413 aliases pays 413 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
